prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1473; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Reviewed first notice of loss. Insured reports vehicle was struck while turning left at an intersection. Other driver's vehicle appears to have been proceeding straight through on the green signal. Police report requested. No lawyer identified for the claimant at this time.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant reports neck and back pain following the collision and says she was evaluated at an urgent care facility. Claimant is not represented and asked how the claim process works. Explained the general steps and that medical documentation will be needed. Requested copies of all treatment records and bills.

Entry 3: Received photos of both vehicles from insured and claimant. Damage to the left front of insured vehicle and the right side of claimant vehicle is consistent with the reported angle of impact. Vehicle inspection scheduled with appraiser. Witness statement from pedestrian at corner obtained and placed in file.

Entry 4: Traffic signal timing records for the intersection requested from the municipality. Insured's statement on the left turn is consistent with the initial report, though insured states the oncoming vehicle was not visible until the last moment. Liability currently leaning toward the insured based on available evidence. Supervisor notified for review.

Entry 5: Claimant provided medical records showing diagnosis of cervical and lumbar strain with recommended physical therapy. Reviewed records and documented injury for evaluation. Claimant still unrepresented and has been advised she may consult an attorney if she wishes. Reserve reviewed and adjusted pending further treatment information. Follow-up call scheduled.
